mainTopic: The כהן גדול's garments, the aggadah of the three role models for learning תורה (הלל, רבי אלעזר בן חרסום, יוסף), and the כהן גדול's first וידוי over his פר
overview: The amud opens with a challenge from a פסוק in יחזקאל: does 'בגדים אחרים' mean the כהן גדול's later garments must be more valuable? The גמרא answers that אחרים can just as well mean less valuable. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a כהן whose mother made him a כתונת may wear it for an עבודת יחיד, as long as he truly hands it over to the ציבור. The גמרא backs this up with the story of רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי. It then tells of רבי אלעזר בן חרסום, whose very fine כתונת made him look undressed, and אביי explains this with the image of wine seen through glass. Because רבי אלעזר was so rich, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about the heavenly court, where the poor, the rich and the wicked must explain why they did not learn תורה. הלל answers the poor, רבי אלעזר בן חרסום answers the rich, and יוסף, who resisted אשת פוטיפר, answers the wicked. Finally, a new משנה returns to the יום הכיפורים service. The כהן גדול leans on his פר and says his first וידוי, and the people answer ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.

steps.title: Challenge from יחזקאל: are the 'other' garments more important?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק saying the כהנים put on 'other garments.' It suggests that 'other' means more important than the first set.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'And they shall put on other garments, so that they do not sanctify the people with their garments.' Doesn't 'other' mean more important than the first ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier position, which matches the משנה's prices, that the later set of garments may be of lower value. It brings a פסוק that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל speaks of the כהנים changing into בגדים אחרים. The challenger reads the word אחרים as meaning a different, higher grade of garment. If that reading holds, the later garments would have to be more valuable, not less.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean...? (pushes toward a reading)

phrases.english: They objected: 'And they shall put on other garments,'
so that they do not sanctify the people with their garments.'
Doesn't 'other' mean more important than them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position on the previous amud that the later garments may be of lesser value.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the later set of garments is less valuable than the first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls the second set אחרים, which the challenger reads as a higher-grade set.

steps.title: No: 'other' can mean less valuable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. אחרים can mean garments of lower value.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Other' means less valuable than them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge by reading the same word the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אחרים only tells us the garments are different. It does not say whether they are better or worse. So the פסוק is no proof, and the earlier position stands.

phrases.english: No, 'other' means inferior to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in step 1.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenger assumed אחרים must mean better, but it can just as well mean worse.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק's word אחרים is open to both readings, so it does not prove the later garments are more valuable.

steps.title: A כתונת made by the כהן's mother may be used once given to the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that once the public service is finished, a כהן may wear a כתונת his mother made him for an עבודת יחיד. The condition is that he hands it over to the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה taught, and some say רב שמואל בר יהודה: After the public service is finished, a כהן whose mother made him a tunic may wear it and do an individual service in it, as long as he gives it over to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It allows a כהן to use a privately made כתונת, on condition that it becomes public property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garments used in the עבודה must belong to the ציבור. So a private garment is allowed only after the כהן transfers ownership to the ציבור. The permission is also limited to an עבודת יחיד performed after the עבודת ציבור is over.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda taught,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda:
After the public service has ended,
a kohen whose mother made him a tunic —
may wear it and perform an individual service in it,
provided he hands it over to the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new related teaching about the garments of the עבודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A privately made כתונת may be used for an עבודת יחיד after the public service, once it is handed over to the ציבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the key requirement is public ownership, not where the garment came from.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to teach this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Obviously!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new information this ruling adds. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the garment is given to the ציבור, it is public property like any other donation. So why would we think it is forbidden? The גמרא is looking for the חידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (asking what the חידוש is)

phrases.english: Isn't this obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's need to state the ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A garment given to the ציבור is clearly public property, so nothing new seems to be taught.

steps.title: The worry he won't give it away fully
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have worried the כהן would not truly hand over a garment he personally wears. The ברייתא teaches that this is not a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should worry that he won't hand it over wholeheartedly. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 4 by naming the worry the ברייתא comes to remove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since his own mother made it and he is the one wearing it, we might suspect he secretly wants to keep owning it. The ברייתא tells us not to worry: a transfer to the ציבור works.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: You might have said: let us be concerned
that perhaps he will not hand it over wholeheartedly;
therefore it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have suspected that the כהן does not truly give up ownership.
steps.terutzMaskana: The transfer is effective, so the garment may be used.

steps.title: The story of רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי's costly tunic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי's mother made him a כתונת worth one hundred מנה. He wore it for an עבודת יחיד and gave it to the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי that his mother made him a tunic worth one hundred מנה. He wore it, performed an individual service in it, and handed it over to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case that matches the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a very expensive garment, which a person would be tempted to keep, was given to the ציבור. This shows in practice what the ברייתא teaches: the transfer works, and the garment can then be used for an עבודת יחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him (introducing a story)
A unit of money (one hundred זוז)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן פִּאָבִי
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Yishmael ben Pabi

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעָשְׂתָה לוֹ אִמּוֹ כְּתוֹנֶת שֶׁל מֵאָה מָנֶה,
phrases.english: that his mother made him a tunic worth one hundred maneh,
and he wore it and performed an individual service in it,
and he handed it over to the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן פִּאָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the ruling of step 3 with an actual case.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a privately made כתונת may be used once handed over to the ציבור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי.
steps.whatToRemember: A privately made כתונת may be used for an עבודת יחיד once it is truly handed over to the ציבור. רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי did this even with a very expensive one.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן חרסום's see-through tunic
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן חרסום's mother made him a כתונת worth twenty thousand. The other כהנים did not let him wear it because he looked undressed in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי אלעזר בן חרסום that his mother made him a tunic worth twenty thousand. His brothers the כהנים did not let him wear it, because he looked as if he were undressed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about a mother who made her son an expensive כתונת. This one has a twist: he was not allowed to wear it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי's tunic from the last step. Here, though, the garment was so fine that wearing it was improper. The detail about it looking see-through sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן גדול who was famously wealthy

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Elazar ben Charsum

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעָשְׂתָה לוֹ אִמּוֹ כְּתוֹנֶת מִשְׁתֵּי רִיבּוֹא,
phrases.english: that his mother made him a tunic worth twenty thousand,
and his brothers the priests did not let him wear it
because he looked like someone undressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רבי ישמעאל בן פאבי's tunic, but with the opposite outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extremely fine כתונת that made the כהן look undressed was not allowed to be worn.

steps.title: How could a priestly tunic be see-through?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the tunic could look see-through, since priestly garment threads were six-fold thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it really be seen through? But the Master said that their threads were doubled six times!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. Priestly garments were woven from six-ply thread, so how could anyone see through one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that the threads of the בגדי כהונה were 'כפול ששה,' made of six strands twisted together. A cloth made from such thick thread should not be transparent. So the story seems to contradict that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But could it be seen? (a challenge)
But didn't the Master say? (introduces a contradicting source)
Their thread is doubled six times

phrases.english: And could it be seen through?
But the Master said: Their thread is six-fold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the factual claim in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר בן חרסום looked undressed in his כתונת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Six-ply thread makes a thick cloth, so it could not be see-through.

steps.title: אביי: like wine seen through glass
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the body was not actually visible. Like wine in a glass cup, its color showed through.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was like wine in a glass cup.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He explains that the tunic was translucent, not truly see-through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The glass keeps the wine covered, yet the wine's color still shows through it. In the same way, the linen was so fine that his skin tone showed, even though his body was not actually exposed. That alone was enough for the other כהנים to call it improper.
steps.whatToRemember: The six-fold thread rule stands. The tunic was not see-through, but the color of his skin showed, like wine through glass.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Like wine in a glass cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא by redefining what 'looked undressed' means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the case: translucent rather than transparent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His body was literally visible through the cloth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only his skin color showed through, like wine in glass.

steps.title: Poverty is no excuse: 'Were you poorer than Hillel?'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the poor, the rich and the wicked all face judgment. A poor person who says he was too busy earning a living is asked, 'Were you poorer than הלל?'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a poor man, a rich man and a wicked man come to judgment. They ask the poor man, 'Why did you not learn תורה?' If he says, 'I was poor and busy earning my food,' they say to him, 'Were you any poorer than הלל?'
steps.whatsHappening: Because רבי אלעזר בן חרסום was so rich, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about rich and poor people judged in שמים. This step gives the poor person's part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up a heavenly trial where each person's excuse for not learning תורה is tested. The poor man's excuse is that he had no time or money. The court answers by pointing to הלל, which sets up the story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Come to judgment (in the heavenly court)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A poor man, a rich man, and a wicked man come to judgment,
To the poor man they say:
Why did you not engage in Torah?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אוֹמֵר: עָנִי הָיִיתִי, וְטָרוּד בִּמְזוֹנוֹתַי,
phrases.english: If he says: I was poor and busy with my sustenance,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: כְּלוּם עָנִי הָיִיתָ יוֹתֵר מֵהִלֵּל?
phrases.english: they say to him: Were you any poorer than Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עָנִי וְעָשִׁיר וְרָשָׁע בָּאִין לַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Branches off, by association with רבי אלעזר בן חרסום's wealth, into a ברייתא about rich and poor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poverty does not excuse a person from learning תורה. הלל is the proof.

steps.title: הלל's daily wage and the skylight
steps.stepSummary: הלל earned a small coin each day and paid half of it to enter the בית המדרש. One day he had no earnings and was not let in, so he climbed onto the skylight to listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about הלל הזקן that every day he worked and earned a טרפעיק (a half-dinar). He gave half to the guard of the בית המדרש, and half went to support himself and his household. One time he found no work, and the guard would not let him in. He climbed up, hung himself over the edge, and sat at the opening of the skylight, so he could hear the words of the living God from שמעיה and אבטליון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the story behind 'Were you poorer than הלל?' It shows how poor הלל was and how far he went to learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל lived on half of a tiny wage and spent the other half just to get into the בית המדרש. When he had nothing at all, he still did not stop learning; he found another way to hear the שיעור. This backs up the ברייתא's claim that poverty is no excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin, half a dinar
The guard of the study hall
A skylight, an opening in the roof
The leading sages of that generation, הלל's teachers

phrases.english: They said about Hillel the Elder
that each and every day he would work
and earn a half-dinar coin,

phrases.aramaic: חֶצְיוֹ הָיָה נוֹתֵן לְשׁוֹמֵר בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: half of it he would give to the guard of the study hall,
and half for his own living and the living of his household.
One time he did not find work to earn,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִנִּיחוֹ שׁוֹמֵר בֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ לְהִכָּנֵס.
phrases.english: and the guard of the study hall did not let him enter.

phrases.aramaic: עָלָה וְנִתְלָה וְיָשַׁב עַל פִּי אֲרוּבָּה
phrases.english: He went up, hung himself over, and sat at the opening of the skylight
in order to hear the words of the living God
from the mouths of Shemaya and Avtalyon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the story that the ברייתא's question about הלל points to.
steps.raayaObject: Poverty is no excuse for not learning תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of הלל's daily wage and his climbing onto the skylight.

steps.title: Snow on Friday night and the darkened hall
steps.stepSummary: It was ערב שבת in the winter month of טבת, and snow fell on הלל all night. At dawn שמעיה noticed the hall was dark, and they saw a human shape in the skylight.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: that day was ערב שבת, in the season of טבת, and snow fell on him from the sky. When dawn came, שמעיה said to אבטליון: 'אבטליון, my brother, every day the house is bright, and today it is dark. Is it a cloudy day?' They looked up and saw the shape of a person in the skylight.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues and becomes more dramatic. הלל stayed on the roof through a snowy winter night until his teachers noticed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These details make the proof stronger. הלל kept learning through freezing cold and snow, overnight into שבת morning. His body was blocking the light from the skylight, which is how his teachers discovered him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיָה,
phrases.english: They said: That day was Shabbat eve,
and it was the season of Tevet,
and snow fell on him from the sky.
When dawn rose
Shemaya said to Avtalyon:
Avtalyon, my brother,

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם הַבַּיִת מֵאִיר וְהַיּוֹם אָפֵל,
phrases.english: every day the house is bright, and today it is dark,
perhaps it is a cloudy day?

phrases.aramaic: הֵצִיצוּ עֵינֵיהֶן וְרָאוּ דְּמוּת אָדָם בַּאֲרוּבָּה.
phrases.english: They looked up and saw the shape of a person in the skylight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the הלל story with the snow and his discovery.
steps.raayaSupportSource: He stayed through a snowy winter night on the skylight.

steps.title: הלל is rescued: worthy of desecrating שבת
steps.stepSummary: They dug הלל out from under three אמות of snow, washed him, rubbed him with oil and warmed him by a fire. They said he was worthy of having שבת desecrated for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went up and found three אמות of snow on him. They took him down, washed him, rubbed him with oil and sat him by the fire. They said: 'This man is worthy of having שבת desecrated for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with הלל's rescue on שבת morning and his teachers' praise of him. This closes the proof that poverty is no excuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting a fire and the other rescue actions are normally forbidden on שבת. Saving a life always permits them. The sages' remark is extra praise: someone this devoted to תורה is especially deserving of it.

keyTerms.meaning: They took him out (of the snow)

steps.whatToRemember: No one can claim 'I was too poor to learn.' הלל had nothing and still risked his life to hear תורה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rescue was allowed only because הלל was special. פיקוח נפש overrides שבת for anyone in danger. 'ראוי זה' is praise, not the legal reason. Also, the story began on ערב שבת, but the rescue took place at dawn, which was already שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the classic answer, at the heavenly judgment, to anyone who claims poverty kept him from learning תורה.

phrases.aramaic: עָלוּ וּמָצְאוּ עָלָיו רוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת שֶׁלֶג.
phrases.english: They went up and found on him snow three cubits high.
They extricated him, washed him, and anointed him with oil,
and sat him opposite the bonfire.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: רָאוּי זֶה לְחַלֵּל עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: They said: This one is worthy to desecrate Shabbat for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: רָאוּי זֶה לְחַלֵּל עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הלל story and seals the ברייתא's point about the poor man.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלל's self-sacrifice proves that poverty is no excuse for neglecting תורה.

steps.title: The rich person's excuse is answered
steps.stepSummary: The heavenly court asks a rich person why he did not learn תורה. He says he was busy with his property. They answer: 'Were you richer than רבי אלעזר?'
steps.simpleTranslation: The court says to a rich person: 'Why did you not learn תורה?' If he says, 'I was rich and busy with my property,' they say to him: 'Were you any richer than רבי אלעזר?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from the poor person to the second person on trial, the rich person, and rejects his excuse. This sets up the story of רבי אלעזר that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern matches the poor person and הלל exactly: an excuse, then a counter-example. The rich man claims that managing his wealth took all his time. The court names someone far richer who still learned, so the excuse falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: 'Were you really...?' A rhetorical opener

phrases.english: A rich person, they say to him:
Why did you not engage in Torah?
If he says: I was rich
and I was busy with my possessions,
they say to him: Were you any richer
than Rabbi Elazar?

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשִׁיר, אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא עָסַקְתָּ בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the poor person (answered by הלל) to the second case in the ברייתא, the rich person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being rich and busy with property is not an acceptable excuse for not learning תורה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן חרסום's great wealth and his travels to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר inherited a thousand villages and a thousand ships. Even so, every day he carried a sack of flour and traveled from place to place to learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי אלעזר בן חרסום that his father left him a thousand villages on land and, matching them, a thousand ships at sea. Every day he took a sack of flour on his shoulder and walked from city to city and from country to country to learn תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains who רבי אלעזר was, to show why he is the perfect answer to the rich man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details work together. His wealth was enormous: villages and ships. Yet he lived like a poor traveler, carrying only plain flour so he could keep moving to wherever there was תורה to learn.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom
that his father left him
a thousand villages on land,
and matching them, a thousand ships at sea.
And each and every day

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל נֹאד שֶׁל קֶמַח עַל כְּתֵיפוֹ
phrases.english: he takes a sack of flour on his shoulder
and walks from city to city
and from country to country to learn Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the court's answer to the rich man by describing רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That even great wealth does not excuse neglecting תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The account of רבי אלעזר בן חרסום's inheritance and his daily travel to learn.

steps.title: His own servants force him into labor
steps.stepSummary: His servants did not recognize him and forced him to work. When he begged to go learn, they swore by the life of רבי אלעזר בן חרסום, their master and the very man they were speaking to, that they would not let him go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once his servants found him and forced him into labor. He said to them, 'Please, let me go so I can learn תורה.' They said, 'By the life of רבי אלעזר בן חרסום, we will not let you go!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how far רבי אלעזר stayed from his own property. His servants had no idea what their master looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The irony proves the point. He was so devoted to learning that his workers had never seen him. Rather than reveal who he was and use his power, he simply asked to be released so he could learn.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By the life of...', a form of oath

steps.confusionAlert: The servants are not mocking him. They swear by their master's life without knowing that the man in front of them IS their master.

phrases.english: One time his servants found him,
and forced him into labor.
He said to them: Please, I beg you,
leave me and I will go learn Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חַיֵּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם
phrases.english: They said to him: By the life of Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom
we will not leave you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that shows how completely רבי אלעזר set his wealth aside.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר ignored his property entirely for the sake of תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of his servants failing to recognize him.

steps.title: He never once went to see his property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the story: רבי אלעזר never went to see his estates. He sat and learned day and night.
steps.simpleTranslation: In all his days he never went to see them (his possessions). Instead, he sat and learned תורה all day and all night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the רבי אלעזר section with a summary line that explains the servants story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains why the servants did not recognize him: he had never visited. It also completes the answer to the rich man. If someone with a thousand villages could leave them alone, an ordinary rich person has no excuse.
steps.whatToRemember: The rich person's excuse is answered by רבי אלעזר בן חרסום, who owned a fortune yet never looked at it, so that he could learn day and night.

phrases.english: And in all his days he never went and saw them,
rather he sits and engages in Torah
all day and all night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up and explains the servants story, closing the rich man's section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wealth is no excuse. רבי אלעזר בן חרסום gave up even looking at his fortune in order to learn constantly.

steps.title: The wicked person's excuse is answered
steps.stepSummary: The court asks a רשע why he did not learn. He says he was handsome and struggled with his יצר. They answer: 'Were you more handsome than יוסף?'
steps.simpleTranslation: The court says to a wicked person: 'Why did you not learn תורה?' If he says, 'I was handsome and busy fighting my יצר,' they say to him: 'Were you any more handsome than יוסף?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the third person on trial, the רשע, and rejects his excuse. This sets up the story of יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the excuse is temptation rather than money or poverty. He claims his good looks brought so many temptations that he could not focus on תורה. The court points to יוסף, who was more handsome and faced harder temptation, yet stayed righteous.

phrases.english: A wicked person, they say to him:
Why did you not engage in Torah?
If he said: I was handsome,
and busy with my inclination,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: כְּלוּם נָאֶה הָיִיתָ מִיּוֹסֵף?
phrases.english: they say to him: Were you any more handsome than Yosef?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָשָׁע, אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא עָסַקְתָּ בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rich person to the third case in the ברייתא, the רשע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strong temptation from one's desires is not an acceptable excuse for not learning תורה.

steps.title: אשת פוטיפר tempted יוסף every day
steps.stepSummary: Every day אשת פוטיפר tried to persuade יוסף with words. She changed her clothes morning and evening to tempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about יוסף הצדיק: every single day אשת פוטיפר tried to win him over with words. The clothes she wore for him in the morning she did not wear in the evening, and the clothes she wore in the evening she did not wear in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins describing how intense יוסף's temptation was, to back up the court's answer to the רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The temptation was constant: every day, with words. It was also always fresh, since she never repeated an outfit. This shows the pressure on יוסף was far greater than what any ordinary person faces.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of פוטיפר, יוסף's Egyptian master

phrases.english: They said about Yosef the righteous:
Each and every day
Potiphar's wife would try to seduce him with words.
Clothes that she wore for him in the morning
she did not wear for him in the evening.
Clothes that she wore for him in the evening
she did not wear for him in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the court's answer to the רשע by describing יוסף's temptation.
steps.raayaObject: That even extreme temptation does not excuse sin or neglect of תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The account of אשת פוטיפר's daily attempts to seduce יוסף.

steps.title: יוסף answers every threat with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: She demanded that יוסף give in, and he refused. She threatened him with prison, with bending him over in suffering, and with blinding. He answered each threat with a פסוק from תהלים about ה׳'s help.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said, 'Listen to me!' He said, 'No.' She said, 'I will lock you in prison!' He said, 'ה׳ frees prisoners.' 'I will bend your posture!' 'ה׳ straightens those who are bent.' 'I will blind your eyes!' 'ה׳ opens the eyes of the blind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves from temptation to threats. יוסף stays firm, trusting in ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each threat is matched by a phrase from תהלים קמ״ו. The point is that fear did not move יוסף, because he trusted that ה׳ could undo any harm she might cause.

keyTerms.meaning: Listen to me (give in to me)
Straightens those who are bent over
Opens the eyes of the blind

phrases.english: She said to him: Listen to me!
He said to her: No.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: הֲרֵינִי חוֹבַשְׁתְּךָ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין!
phrases.english: She said to him: I will lock you up in prison!
He said to her: "God releases prisoners."
I will bend your stature!
"God straightens the bent."
I will blind your eyes!
"God opens the eyes of the blind."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the pressure from words and clothing to direct demands and threats.
steps.raayaObject: That יוסף resisted even under threats of harm.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dialogue between אשת פוטיפר and יוסף, with פסוקים from תהלים.

steps.title: Even a huge bribe could not move יוסף
steps.stepSummary: She offered יוסף a thousand silver talents to be with her, and he still refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: She gave him a thousand talents of silver to listen to her, "to lie with her, to be with her," and he refused to listen to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a final test, money, and יוסף refuses that too. This closes the answer to the רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She tried every tactic: words, beauty, threats, and finally a fortune. יוסף stood firm against all of them. Since he resisted far more than any ordinary person faces, the רשע's excuse is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Talents of silver (a very large sum)
To lie with her (quoting בראשית ל״ט:י׳)

steps.whatToRemember: יוסף withstood words, threats and even a fortune in silver, so temptation cannot excuse a person.

phrases.english: She gave him a thousand talents of silver
to listen to her,
"to lie with her, to be with her,"
and he did not want to listen to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתְנָה לוֹ אֶלֶף כִּכְּרֵי כֶסֶף לִשְׁמוֹעַ אֵלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the יוסף story with a final bribe that he refuses, completing the answer to the רשע.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יוסף resisted temptation, threats, and bribery. A person's desires cannot excuse sin or neglect of תורה.
steps.raayaObject: That even extreme temptation does not excuse sin or neglect of תורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יוסף refused a thousand talents of silver offered by אשת פוטיפר.

steps.title: Why יוסף refused: this world and the next
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק's double wording, 'to lie with her' and 'to be with her,' is read as this world and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To lie with her' means in this world. 'To be with her' means in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק about יוסף uses two phrases. Giving in for a moment in this world would have tied him to her in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יוסף would not listen to her 'לשכב אצלה להיות עמה.' The גמרא reads the extra phrase as a second, deeper result: sin in this world would bind him to her forever in the next world. This explains why even a thousand talents could not move him.

keyTerms.meaning: To lie with her (words from the פסוק)
To be with her (words from the פסוק)

phrases.english: "To lie with her" in this world,
"To be with her" in the World-to-Come.
phrases.notes: The second half of the verse is read as what comes of it forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind יוסף's refusal described in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two phrases in the פסוק mean this world and עולם הבא. A sin of this world would have bound יוסף to her forever.

steps.title: Three role models leave no one an excuse
steps.stepSummary: הלל obligates the poor, רבי אלעזר בן חרסום obligates the rich, and יוסף obligates the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes out that הלל obligates the poor, רבי אלעזר בן חרסום obligates the wealthy, and יוסף obligates the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the whole story section. Each of the three stories answers a different excuse for not learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person cannot say he was too busy earning a living, because הלל learned even in poverty. A rich person cannot say his business kept him busy, because of רבי אלעזר בן חרסום. A person drawn to sin cannot blame his יצר, because יוסף overcame a far greater test.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligates (here: proves someone guilty for not learning)
Wicked people (here: those who claim their יצר beat them)

steps.whatToRemember: No excuse works in the Heavenly court. Poverty (הלל), wealth (רבי אלעזר בן חרסום), and temptation (יוסף) each have a role model who still learned or stayed loyal.

phrases.english: Consequently, Hillel obligates the poor,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם מְחַיֵּיב אֶת הָעֲשִׁירִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Harsum obligates the wealthy,
Joseph obligates the wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the aggadic section by drawing the lesson from all three stories.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every type of person has a model who overcame his situation, so no excuse for neglecting תורה will be accepted.

steps.title: The כהן גדול leans on his bull to confess
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes where the פר and the כהן גדול stood, and how he did סמיכה and וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He comes to his bull. The bull stood between the Entrance Hall and the altar, its head to the south and its face to the west. The priest stands on the east side, facing west. He places his two hands on it and confesses.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and returns to the יום הכיפורים service. It describes the setup for the כהן גדול's first confession over his own פר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives exact positions. The פר stands between the אולם and the מזבח, with its body turned so its face points west, toward the היכל. The כהן גדול stands east of it, also facing west, and does סמיכה with both hands while saying וידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Bull; here the כהן גדול's own חטאת for יום הכיפורים
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל
Leaning one's hands on a קרבן

phrases.english: MISHNA: He comes next to his bull,

phrases.aramaic: וּפָרוֹ הָיָה עוֹמֵד בֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: and his bull was standing between the Entrance Hall and the altar,
its head to the south and its face to the west.
phrases.notes: The body is turned so the face points toward the היכל.

phrases.english: And the priest stands on the east side, with his face to the west.
And he places his two hands on it, and confesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It leaves the aggadah and returns to the יום הכיפורים service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול stands east of his פר, both facing west, leans with both hands, and confesses.

steps.title: The words of the כהן גדול's confession
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the exact text of the וידוי: three kinds of sin, for himself and his household, ending with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he would say: Please, ה׳! I have done iniquity, I have rebelled, I have sinned before You, I and my household. Please, ה׳, grant atonement for the iniquities, the rebellions, and the sins that I and my household committed before You, as it is written in the תורה of משה Your servant: 'For on this day He shall atone for you...'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the exact words the כהן גדול said while leaning on the פר. He first admits the sins, then asks for atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The confession has two parts. First he admits three kinds of wrongdoing: עוון, פשע, and חטא. Then he asks for כפרה for those same three, and he backs up the request with the פסוק promising atonement on יום הכיפורים. This first confession covers only himself and 'ביתי,' his household.
steps.confusionAlert: Where the text says 'אנא השם,' the כהן גדול actually pronounced ה׳'s real Name (the שם המפורש). Also, the order עויתי, פשעתי, חטאתי is not the final word. The גמרא will soon discuss which order is correct.

phrases.english: And this is what he would say:
Please, ה׳! I have done iniquity, I have rebelled,
phrases.notes: He actually said the Divine Name here.

phrases.english: I have sinned before You, I and my household.
Please, ה׳! Grant atonement, please,
for the iniquities, and for the rebellions, and for the sins
that I have done in iniquity, and in rebellion, and in sin
before You, I and my household,
as it is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant:
"For on this day He shall atone, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual words of the וידוי mentioned at the end of step 24.
steps.whyThisMatters: This text is the model for the יום הכיפורים confession. The order of עוון, פשע, and חטא becomes a debate in the גמרא that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול confesses עוון, פשע, and חטא for himself and his household, then asks for כפרה, citing the פסוק.

steps.title: The people answer with ברוך שם
steps.stepSummary: After hearing the Name, the people respond: ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they answer after him: 'Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by describing how the כהנים and the people in the עזרה respond when they hear the כהן גדול say ה׳'s Name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית המקדש, people did not answer אמן. Instead they answered ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד. They said it out of honor when the שם המפורש was spoken.

keyTerms.term: בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
keyTerms.meaning: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever

steps.whatToRemember: The first וידוי: the כהן גדול stands east of his פר and leans with both hands. He confesses for himself and his household and asks for כפרה with the פסוק. The people respond ברוך שם when they hear the Name.

phrases.english: And they respond after him:
"Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the confession scene with the people's response.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the שם המפורש is spoken in the confession, those present answer ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד.
